sentences.text:
This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code praying for quashing of First Information Report in Crime No.1034/2022 and the consequent Final Report/Charge-sheet No.128/2023 dated 17.3.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 5 of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887.

As per the contents of the said First Information Report the respondent No.2 on receiving secret information conducted raid on the house of one Sachin Yerone residing at Saturna area wherein it was found that said Sachin was indulged in the activity of cricket betting, as the match between India and New Zealand was going on.
It was found that said Sachin with the aid of cellphones was doing betting.
Two cellphones and chargers were found from his person and an offence came to be registered against them under Sections mentioned above.
After completion of investigation the prosecution filed a charge-sheet in the matter.
The present application was accordingly amended and the charge-sheet so filed was also challenged.

3. We have heard Mr. R.J. Shinde, learned counsel for the applicant and Mr. N.B. Jawade, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1.
4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that no offence is made out from the meaningful reading of the First Information Report in question and there is nothing incriminating even in the charge-sheet filed by the prosecution after completion of investigation.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, vehemently opposed the submissions made by the counsel for the applicant and states that there is enough material on record to show the involvement of the applicant in the offences.

He further submits that the mobile panchanama of the applicant clearly reveals incriminating material and, therefore, there is a material veracity which would adjudicated in a full fledged criminal trial.
He, therefore, submits for rejection of the application.
5. As can be seen from the First Information Report in question, raid was conducted on the premises belonging to the applicant two mobile phones were seized from him.
After doing panchanama of the said mobile phones, it was found that the applicant is indulged in online betting and accepting bids from the public.
It is, therefore, clear that the applicant for his financial gain is inducing the public and making them bid on the cricket matches to be held.
6. It is, therefore, difficult to accept the contentions of the learned counsel for the applicant about the absence of any material against the applicant/accused.
7. It is, therefore, clear that there is a prima facie material against the accused i.e. the present applicant.

It is, therefore, clear that there is prima facie material against the applicant and,
therefore, it would not be a fit case to quash the First Information Report as far the present applicant is concerned.
ORDER The application is, therefore, rejected.
(Nandesh S. Deshpande, J.) (Urmila Joshi-Phalke, J.) wadode Signed by: Mr. Devendra Wadode
